It is the mental-state element of burglary in US and common-law jurisdictions: the defendant must intend, at the moment of unlawful entry into a building, to commit a felony inside, and the intent need not be carried out. Intent is usually inferred from conduct and circumstances. In England and Wales the equivalent is Theft Act 1968 s.9(1)(a), which requires entry as a trespasser with intent to commit theft, grievous bodily harm, or criminal damage.
